data.name: Diagnostics.Logs.Help.Html
data.value: {0} writes a line to {1}, prefixed with the mod id. A failing callback (event, timer or keybind) is logged with the mod, the event and the error, never stops the other subscribers, and disables its subscription after {2} consecutive failures.

data.value: {0} without arguments returns the state and the running interval's sections.

data.name: Diagnostics.Telemetry.Report.Html
data.value: To ask for a report, a user with a large setup adds a small mod that enables telemetry, plays one mission and sends {0}. The checks below the editor warn while a script turns telemetry on, so it does not end up in a published mod by accident.

data.name: Diagnostics.Telemetry.Sections
data.value: Every report interval, Runtime then logs the average, p95, p99 and maximum of its whole per-frame update, of one ensure byte-check and of event polling, with the active ensures and re-applications. Disabled, it costs one boolean test per timed section; timing needs the game's precise clock (in game).

data.name: Diagnostics.WriteConflicts.HeldBy.Html
data.value: Since HD2Runtime 0.30 a CONFLICT line says who holds the bytes ({0} names the mod, operation and value) and {1} lists every other target of that record. Keep one of the two edits, or give both the same value: equal values compose.
data.comment: {0}, {1}: Runtime log phrases, kept in English

data.name: Diagnostics.WriteConflicts.How.Html
data.value: An {0} keeps its target at the value it wrote and re-checks only the bytes it owns. When those bytes changed while their allocation is still the reviewed one, something else wrote them: Runtime re-applies its value and counts the change for that operation.

data.name: Diagnostics.WriteConflicts.ModBuilder.Html
data.value: Operation ids that start with {0} are the edits ModBuilder generated.

data.name: Diagnostics.WriteConflicts.NotCounted
data.value: A game reallocation is not a write conflict: the game rebuilt its data, and Runtime re-resolves it the normal way. The counting runs only on a detected drift, never per frame.
data.comment: Diagnostics reference: what is not counted, and the cost.

data.name: Diagnostics.WriteConflicts.Reading
data.value: Two mods writing the same bytes fight: each re-applies its own value, Runtime at most once per verification interval. If a report shows conflicts, remove one of the two mods (or one of the two edits); if it shows none, a frame-rate loss is not Runtime fighting another writer.
data.comment: Diagnostics reference: how to read a write-conflict report.

data.name: Diagnostics.WriteConflicts.Warning
data.value: After 3 external changes within the operation's window (five of its verification intervals, at least 10 s), Runtime logs one line naming the operation, its target and up to four fields, the count and the time span. The next warning for that operation waits a full window.
data.comment: Diagnostics reference: when the write-conflict warning is logged.
